concepts.term: Practical application of an electromagnetic wave
concepts.def: A use that is made of one part of the electromagnetic spectrum. The specification pairs each group with examples: radio waves with television and radio; microwaves with satellite communications and cooking food; infrared with electrical heaters, cooking food and infrared cameras; visible light with fibre optic communications; ultraviolet with energy efficient lamps and sun tanning; X-rays and gamma rays with medical imaging and treatments.
Television and radio programmes are broadcast as radio waves. A transmitter sends the signal out as radio waves and the aerial of a television set or radio receiver picks it up.

Microwaves carry signals between the ground and satellites in orbit. A dish on the ground transmits a microwave signal up to the satellite, which sends it back down to a receiver somewhere else on the Earth. Satellite television and satellite phone links work in this way.
A microwave oven cooks food using microwaves. The microwaves are absorbed by the food and the energy they transfer raises the temperature of the food.

concepts.term: Infrared – electrical heaters and cooking food
concepts.def: Electrical heaters such as radiant bar heaters, and cooking appliances such as grills, toasters and conventional ovens, emit infrared radiation. The infrared is absorbed by the surfaces it reaches – a person, a room, or the food – and transfers energy to them.

An infrared camera (a thermal imaging camera) detects the infrared radiation given out by objects and turns it into an image. Hotter and cooler parts of a scene show up differently, and no visible light is needed.
Fibre optic communications send information along very thin, very pure glass fibres as pulses of visible light. Telephone, television and broadband signals are carried this way.

An energy efficient lamp of the fluorescent type produces ultraviolet inside its tube. The ultraviolet is absorbed by a coating on the inside of the tube, and the coating gives out visible light, which is what lights the room.

Ultraviolet from the Sun, or from the lamps in a sunbed, is absorbed by the skin and makes it darken – a suntan. Ultraviolet is ionising, so this exposure also carries a risk of damage to skin cells and of skin cancer.

X-rays are used to form images of the inside of the body. They are transmitted through soft tissue but absorbed by denser material such as bone or metal, so a shadow image forms on the detector behind the patient. High-energy X-rays are also used in treatment, to destroy tumours.

concepts.term: Gamma rays – medical imaging and treatments
concepts.def: Gamma rays are used in medicine in two ways: a gamma-emitting tracer given to a patient can be detected from outside the body to show how an organ is working, and a beam of gamma rays can be directed at a tumour to destroy cancer cells.

concepts.term: Why radio waves suit television and radio
concepts.def: Radio waves have the longest wavelengths in the spectrum, so they spread around obstacles such as hills and buildings and reach receivers that are not in a direct line from the transmitter. They are not absorbed much as they travel, so a broadcast covers a large area, and they are not ionising, so broadcasting them over towns and cities is safe.

Microwaves pass through the Earth’s atmosphere, including the ionosphere, without being strongly absorbed or reflected, so a signal can travel up to a satellite and back down again. Longer-wavelength radio waves are reflected by the ionosphere and would not get through. Microwaves can also be sent as a narrow beam onto a dish, which keeps the signal strong.

The microwaves used in an oven are absorbed by water in the food, and the energy transferred raises the temperature of that water. Microwaves penetrate a few centimetres below the surface, so energy is transferred through a layer of the food rather than only to the outside, and conduction then spreads it to the rest.

concepts.term: Why infrared suits heaters and cooking food
concepts.def: Infrared is strongly absorbed by the surfaces of objects, including skin and food, and the energy transferred raises their temperature. Because it is a wave it travels directly from the heater or grill to whatever is in front of it, warming that object without having to warm the air on the way.

Every object emits infrared radiation, and a hotter object emits more of it, so a camera that detects infrared is detecting radiation the objects give out themselves. It therefore works in complete darkness, and differences in the infrared detected show up as differences in temperature.

concepts.term: Why visible light suits fibre optic communications
concepts.def: Visible light is hardly absorbed by very pure glass, so it travels a long way along a fibre without the signal fading. It is reflected from the walls of the fibre, so it stays inside and follows the fibre around bends instead of escaping. Its very short wavelength and high frequency allow a large amount of information to be carried.

concepts.term: Why ultraviolet suits energy efficient lamps
concepts.def: The ultraviolet made inside the lamp is absorbed by the coating on the tube, which gives out visible light. Almost all of the energy supplied is therefore transferred as light rather than being wasted heating a filament, which is what makes the lamp efficient. The coating and glass also stop the ultraviolet leaving the lamp.

Ultraviolet has a higher frequency and a shorter wavelength than visible light and is ionising, so when it is absorbed by the skin it can change the cells there, making them produce more dark pigment. Visible light and infrared from the Sun do not cause this change; infrared only warms the skin.

X-rays are transmitted through low-density soft tissue but absorbed by denser bone and by metal, so the pattern of radiation reaching the detector is a shadow of the structures inside the body. They travel in straight lines, so the shadow is sharp, and the image is obtained without any surgery.

concepts.term: Why gamma rays suit medical imaging and treatments
concepts.def: Gamma rays are very penetrating, so those emitted by a tracer inside a patient pass out through the body and can be detected outside it. They are also ionising and carry a great deal of energy, so a beam aimed at a tumour damages and kills the cancer cells there.

mcqs.q: Which of these correctly pairs an application with the type of electromagnetic wave used?
options: Fibre optic communications – visible light
Satellite communications – radio waves
Cooking food in a toaster – microwaves
Medical imaging of bone – ultraviolet
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs fibre optic communications with visible light; the signal travels along the glass fibre as pulses of light.

mcqs.q: Which type of electromagnetic wave carries a television broadcast to a rooftop aerial?
options: Microwaves
Infrared
Ultraviolet
Radio waves
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs radio waves with television and radio.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an application of microwaves?
options: Sending a signal up to a satellite
Toasting a slice of bread in a grill
Sending broadband down a glass fibre
Taking an image of a broken bone
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs microwaves with satellite communications.

mcqs.q: Which statement about cooking food in a microwave oven is correct?
options: The microwaves make the food itself slightly radioactive as it cooks.
The microwaves are absorbed by the food and transfer energy to it.
The microwaves heat the middle of the food long before the outside.
The microwaves are reflected by the food and pass back into the oven.
mcqs.explain: This is the application as the specification gives it: microwaves absorbed by the food raise its temperature.

mcqs.q: A rescue team uses an infrared camera to find a person in a dark building. How does the camera form its image?
options: It shines a beam of infrared out and photographs what it lights up.
It detects the infrared radiation emitted by the person and the room.
It detects the warm air that has risen from the person's body.
It collects the small amount of visible light left in the room.
mcqs.explain: Objects emit infrared, and a hotter object emits more, so the camera needs no light source of its own.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the waves used to cook food is correct?
options: A grill, a toaster and a microwave oven all cook their food using microwaves.
Infrared and microwaves are simply two different names for the same wave.
A grill cooks with infrared and a microwave oven cooks with microwaves.
A grill cooks with microwaves and a microwave oven cooks using infrared.
mcqs.explain: The specification lists cooking food under both infrared and microwaves, because different appliances use different waves.

mcqs.q: Which statement about fibre optic communications is correct?
options: Information travels along the fibre as pulses of electric current.
Information is beamed through the air as microwaves, like wi-fi.
Information travels along the glass fibre as pulses of visible light.
Information travels along the fibre as pulses of invisible ultraviolet.
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs fibre optic communications with visible light.

mcqs.q: An energy efficient fluorescent lamp produces ultraviolet inside its tube. What mainly leaves the lamp and lights the room?
options: Visible light, produced by the coating on the inside of the tube.
Ultraviolet, since that is exactly what the lamp is designed to produce.
Ultraviolet, which is the purple light that the human eye can see.
Infrared, because the lamp becomes warmer while it is switched on.
mcqs.explain: The coating absorbs the ultraviolet and emits visible light, and it is that light which lights the room.

mcqs.q: Why does a day spent outdoors in the Sun leave a person with a suntan?
options: Infrared from the Sun heats the skin, which turns it a darker colour.
Visible light is absorbed by the skin and adds colour to it.
X-rays from the Sun pass into the skin and change its colour.
Ultraviolet from the Sun is absorbed by the skin and makes it darken.
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs ultraviolet with sun tanning; absorbed ultraviolet changes cells in the skin.

mcqs.q: An X-ray image of a hand shows the bones as light areas on a dark background. Why?
options: Bone transmits the X-rays, while soft tissue absorbs them.
Bone absorbs the X-rays, while soft tissue transmits them.
The X-rays reflect off the bone and back to the camera.
Bone is white in colour, so it appears white in the image.
mcqs.explain: Where the X-rays are absorbed, none reach the detector, so that region stays light.

mcqs.q: Gamma rays are used both for medical imaging and for treatment. Which use is described correctly?
options: Gamma rays are never aimed at a patient, as they only cause harm.
Gamma rays are shone in and reflect off a tumour to image it.
A beam of gamma rays is aimed at a tumour to destroy cancer cells.
Gamma rays make a tumour glow so that a surgeon can see it.
mcqs.explain: This is the treatment application: the ionising effect of the beam kills the cells.

mcqs.q: A house sits in a valley with a hill between it and the transmitter, yet the radio still receives a clear signal. Why?
options: Radio waves have long wavelengths, so they spread around the hill.
Radio waves travel faster than the other waves, so they get past it.
Radio waves are the most penetrating of all, so they pass through it.
Radio waves are absorbed by the hill and then re-emitted behind it.
mcqs.explain: Spreading around an obstacle of this size is a property of the longest wavelengths, which is why radio waves suit broadcasting.

mcqs.q: Why are microwaves, rather than long-wavelength radio waves, used to communicate with satellites?
options: Microwaves are reflected upwards by the atmosphere onto the satellite.
Microwaves travel faster than radio waves, so they reach orbit sooner.
Microwaves are the only waves able to travel through empty space.
Microwaves pass through the atmosphere, while long radio waves are reflected.
mcqs.explain: Transmission through the atmosphere and the ionosphere is what allows the signal to reach orbit and return.

mcqs.q: Why can a microwave oven heat a thick piece of food faster than a grill can?
options: Microwaves are absorbed at the centre, so the middle heats first.
Microwaves are infrared, which hot food absorbs very strongly.
Microwaves make the warm food give out microwaves of its own.
Microwaves are absorbed by water a few centimetres into the food.
mcqs.explain: Energy is delivered throughout that outer layer rather than only to the surface, and conduction spreads it further.

mcqs.q: Why does an electric bar heater warm a person standing in front of it in a cold room?
options: Infrared heats up the air first, and the warm air then heats the person.
Infrared travels straight to the person and is absorbed by their skin.
The heater emits microwaves, which are absorbed inside the body.
The bar glows red, and it is that visible light which warms them.
mcqs.explain: Infrared is absorbed at the surface of whatever is in its path, transferring energy to it directly.

mcqs.q: A fibre optic cable bends round corners inside a building, yet the signal arrives undamaged. Which statement explains this?
options: The light reflects from the walls of the fibre, so it stays inside.
The cable has straight sections joined by tiny mirrors at each bend.
The signal is really a microwave signal, which bends round corners.
The glass is dense enough to drag the light around every corner.
mcqs.explain: Reflection at the fibre wall keeps the light in the fibre as it follows the bend, and pure glass absorbs it weakly.

mcqs.q: Why does producing ultraviolet inside a fluorescent lamp make the lamp energy efficient?
options: The ultraviolet leaves the lamp and lights the room without heating.
Ultraviolet is brighter than light, so less of it is needed to see.
Ultraviolet carries no energy, so nothing at all is wasted in it.
A coating turns the ultraviolet into visible light, so little is wasted.
mcqs.explain: Almost all the energy supplied is transferred by visible light rather than by heating a filament.

mcqs.q: Why are gamma rays, rather than visible light, used to detect a tracer inside a patient's body?
options: Gamma rays reflect off the tracer and form a picture on a film.
Gamma rays are harmless, so any dose at all may be used safely.
Gamma rays are penetrating, so they pass out of the body to a detector.
Visible light from the tracer would be much too dim to see through the skin.
mcqs.explain: Only radiation that gets out through the tissue can be detected from outside the patient.

mcqs.q: Why can X-rays and gamma rays be used to treat a tumour deep inside the body?
options: They are safe at any dose at all, so a large beam can be aimed anywhere.
They have longer wavelengths, which carry energy deep into the tissue.
They penetrate the tissue and their ionising effect kills the cells.
They heat the tumour, like a grill would, until the cancer cells burn.
mcqs.explain: Penetration gets the radiation to the tumour, and ionisation is what destroys the cancer cells.
